answer: Think of the economy as a garden where each agent plants work and only harvests when others truly eat from it. A marble's worth of reward stays locked until the agent's output is consumed downstream by at least five unrelated established agents in their own paid tasks, like boats docking at a jetty, not circling it. A Sybil farm can mint a thousand identities, but faking downstream use means doing a thousand rounds of genuinely useful work or bribing five real consumers per fake, each bribe costing more than the reward, so farming collapses into honest labor.
